WHEREAS:
The Council is the local planning authority by whom the obligations contained in this
Agreement are enforceable.
The Owner owns the freehold interest in the Site and is registered as proprietor of it with Title
Absolute at the Land Registry free from encumbrances other than those matters contained
or referred to in the Property and Charges Register of Title Number TGL19647 at the date of
this Agreement.
The Lender has a charge over Title Number TGL19647 and has agreed to join into this
Agreement in the manner hereafter provided.
The Owner wishes to construct the Development upon the Site in accordance with the
Planning Permission and the obligations contained herein.
On 23 May 2019 the Owner submitted the Application to the Council and on 15 June 2020
the Council's Planning Committee resolved to grant the Planning Permission subject to the
completion of this Agreement.
Having regard to the provisions of the Development Plan and the planning considerations
affecting the Site, the Council considers that in the interests of the proper planning of its area
the Development of the Site ought only be permitted subject to the terms hereof and for that
purpose the Parties are wiling to enter into this Agreement.

Not to Occupy the Development until the District Heating Network Strategy has been

Network Strategy shall set out as a minimum:
2.1.1 how the Development will be designed and built so that it will be capable of

known or expected and reasonable service entry routes including sleeves, pipework,
reasonable access and space necessary for the purpose of connecting the
Development to the District Heating Network;

be metered;
1 confirmation that the pipework to each Residential Unit and commercial units will be
fitted with isolation valves and a heat meter so that consumption of energy can be
monitored (if such technology is available for use at a reasonable cost);
confirmation that allowance has been made within the Development for hot water
generation by way of heat exchangers connected to the District Heating Network and
energy centre; and
as far as practical, confirmation that the necessary equipment, plants, ducts or routes
for pipes, meters, materials and other technology reasonably required (including plate
heat exchanger and absorption chiller) are or will be available to facilitate connection
to the District Heating Network.

Strategy referred to in paragraph 2.1 above within 8 weeks of receipt of the same and if the
Council's written response is to the effect that the District Heating Network Strategy is not
approved the Council must set out its reasons for not approving the said strategy and the
parties shall each use reasonable endeavours to discuss and reach agreement to the District
Heating Network Strategy within the period of 8 weeks from the receipt by the Council of the
District Heating Network Strategy or such other period as the parties may agree.
In the event that the District Heating Network Strategy is not agreed within the said 8 week
period then either party may refer the same for determination under clause 19 of this
Agreement.

the Specialist's determination that the District Heating Network Strategy is approved) the
Owner shall carry out the Development in accordance with the approved District Heating
Network Strategy.

three months of receipt of the Connection Notice submit the Feasibility Study to the Council for
approval.In the event that the Feasibility Study is not agreed then either party may refer the
same for determination under clause 19 of this Agreement.
If the parties (acting reasonably) agree that the Feasibility Study dermonstrates that it is
feasible and financially viable for the Development to connect into the District Heating Network
or (failing agreement between the Council and the Owner ) the Specialist pursuant to clause
19 determines that the connection of the Development to the District Heating Network is
feasible and financially viable, then the Owner shall use all reasonable endeavours to connect
the Development to the District Heating Network in accordance with the approved District
Heating Network Strategy (unless otherwise agreed) within a reasonable period following the
date of the joint decision by the Council and the Owner (or where applicable the decision of
the Specialist) that connection is feasible and financially viable.
Carbon Green Fund Contribution
Prior to the Occupation of 50% of the Development (or upon such other date as may be
agreed between the Council and the Owner) the Council and the Owner shall compare the
environmental performance of the Development against the Agreed Carbon Targets and
against the final compliance calculations ("the Assessment").
If the Owner and the Council agree that the Assessment referred to in paragraph 3.1 of this
Schedule may take place then the Owner shall carry out the Assessment and notify the
Council of the proposed quantum of the Carbon Green Fund Contribution based on the
Assessment.
In the event that the actual carbon emissions have improved against the Agreed Carbon
Targets contained in the Site Wide Energy Strategy (and calculated in accordance with the
relevant emissions factors in place at the time of the Assessment) the Owner may reduce the
maximum Carbon Green Fund Contribution by a sum equivalent to £1800 per tonne of annual
residual CO2 emissions for each tonne of annual residual CO2 emissions that are below those
set out in the Site Wide Energy Strategy (and calculated in accordance with the relevant
emissions factor in place at the time of the Assessment).
In the event the quantum of the Carbon Green Fund Contribution is not agreed within 8 weeks
of submission by the Owner of the notice pursuant to paragraph 3.2 then either party may
refer the issue for determination under clause 19 of this Agreement.
The Carbon Green Fund Contribution (as agreed between the Council and the Owner or
determined in accordance with clause 19 of this Agreement) shall be payable within 20
Working Days of such agreement or determination.
